reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Statutory definition of unlawful detainer
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful detainer to include holding over after lease termination, foreclosure after written notice or ten business days after subsection 3 notice, post-employment occupancy, or wrongful disseisin after written demand.

headings.title: Ten-business-day foreclosure vacate notice to residential tenants
headings.reviewNote: Requires a foreclosure purchaser seeking possession from a compliant residential tenant (§ 441.020) to give at least ten business days' notice before filing an action, without creating a tenancy or barring agreement.

headings.title: Mailing, door posting, and form of foreclosure occupant notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires certified/registered mail (or regular mail to 'occupant' if unnamed) with specified envelope wording, posting on the dwelling door, and prescribed statutory notice text.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections and history notes for 534.030. Corrected subsection 2 note ('ninety days' -> 'not less than ten business days') and subsection 3 title/note (door posting is required in addition to mail in all cases, plus prescribed notice text).

headings.title: Verified complaint and issuance of summons
headings.reviewNote: Requires the clerk, upon a signed and sworn written circuit court complaint specifying the property and unlawful or forcible detainer, to issue a summons for appearance on a specified day.

headings.title: Assignment of court date within twenty-one business days
headings.reviewNote: Requires assigning a court date at summons issuance for a day certain not more than twenty-one business days after issuance unless the plaintiff or counsel consents in writing to a later date.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and history notes for 534.070. Removed fabricated 'or thirty days in certain counties' from subsection 2 note.

headings.title: Time for personal service of summons before hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires service of the summons as in other civil cases at least four days before the court date specified in the summons.

headings.title: Service by posting and ordinary mail upon unserved defendant
headings.reviewNote: Directs ten-day posting on the premises and in one public place plus ordinary mail to last known address when ordinary service fails, barring default money judgments under this procedure.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and history notes for 534.090. Refined subsection 2 note to reflect ten-day posting in two locations, ordinary mail, bar on default money judgment, and next available court date when executed.

headings.title: Judgment for restitution, double damages, and double rent
headings.reviewNote: Requires judgment on a complainant's verdict or finding for restitution of the premises, double assessed damages, double monthly rents and profits from judgment until restitution, and costs.

headings.title: Transmittal of final judgment to enforcing law enforcement agency
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court within two business days after a plaintiff's subsection 1 judgment becomes final to transmit a copy to the law enforcement agency with jurisdiction to enforce it.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and 1972/1974 annotations for 534.330. Replaced fabricated subsection 2 ('local public housing authority') with actual text requiring transmittal of final judgment to the enforcing law enforcement agency within two business days.

headings.title: Definitions under unlawful residential occupancy removal law
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'petitioner', 'respondent', and 'unlawful occupant' or 'unlawful occupants' for purposes of this section.

headings.title: Petition for removal of unlawful occupant from residential dwelling
headings.reviewNote: Permits a property owner or authorized agent to seek removal of unlawful occupants of a residential dwelling by filing a verified petition in the county or St. Louis City where the property lies.

headings.title: Clerk duty to assist and explain removal petition procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires court clerks (except under subsection 6) to assist unrepresented filers without cost, post notices, and directs supreme court forms/instructions without constituting the practice of law (§ 484.010).

headings.title: Filing fees and court costs in unlawful occupancy actions
headings.reviewNote: Sets filing fees and court costs under this section equal to those required when filing a claim in associate circuit court.

headings.title: Immediate ex parte order for removal of unlawful occupants
headings.reviewNote: Directs immediate issuance of an ex parte removal order upon a verified petition setting forth nine required facts showing good cause, with a hearing within 48 hours absent good cause for delay.

headings.title: Protective terms and temporary relief in ex parte removal order
headings.reviewNote: Provides that ex parte orders protect petitioners from trespass and may include safety terms restraining violence (including against pets), entry/proximity, and communication.

headings.title: Additional permanent relief and costs after hearing
headings.reviewNote: Permits a court issuing a post-hearing permanent exclusion order to additionally grant permanent restraints, expulsion of occupant and personal property, repair costs, service costs, and court costs.

headings.title: Required allegations and prayer in verified removal petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires a verified petition seeking an ex parte order under this section to contain allegations relating to those orders and pray for the orders desired.

headings.title: Sheriff enforcement of removal order
headings.reviewNote: Directs the sheriff of the county or St. Louis City where the property is located to enforce a granted order by removing the respondent from the property.

headings.title: Sheriff authority to arrest unlawful occupants for trespass
headings.reviewNote: Permits the sheriff, if appropriate, to arrest any person found in the dwelling for trespass, outstanding warrants, or any other legal cause.

headings.title: Sheriff fees, standby peace-keeping, and property damage immunity
headings.reviewNote: Entitles the sheriff to § 57.280 writ-of-possession fees and reasonable hourly standby rates while locks are changed and property removed, and limits sheriff and owner/agent liability for property damage.

headings.title: Civil cause of action for wrongful removal without just cause
headings.reviewNote: Permits a person removed without just cause to sue for restored possession, actual personal property damages (capped at value), $1,000 statutory damages, and court costs, offset by proven real property damages.

headings.title: Preservation of property owner rights and criminal arrest authority
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section does not limit property owner rights or law enforcement authority to arrest an unlawful occupant for trespassing, vandalism, theft, or other crimes.

headings.title: Cumulative nature of statutory removal proceedings and remedies
headings.reviewNote: Provides that all proceedings under this section are in addition to other available civil or criminal remedies unless otherwise specifically provided.

headings.title: Continuing jurisdiction, compliance hearings, and contempt enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Retains court jurisdiction for the duration of ex parte or full orders, permits compliance review hearings, and makes orders enforceable by judgment remedies and contempt for willful violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 15 subsections and subdivisions for 534.602. Corrected subsection 1 note (three defined terms, excluding 'residential dwelling'), preserved permissive 'may' in subsection 7, aligned subsection 8 with actual text, and expanded subsections 11 and 15 to cover standby peace-keeping/immunity and enforcement/contempt.

headings.title: Mandatory warrantless arrest for violation of ex parte removal order
headings.reviewNote: Requires a law enforcement officer with probable cause that a respondent with notice violated a § 534.602 ex parte order to arrest the respondent whether or not committed in the officer's presence.

headings.title: Immunity of law enforcement officers acting in good faith
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil immunity from false arrest, false imprisonment, or malicious prosecution claims to arresting/assisting officers, employing entities, and superiors acting in good faith reliance on this section.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty and deemed notice of ex parte order
headings.reviewNote: Makes violation of a § 534.602 ex parte order a class A misdemeanor and deems a party to have notice if a responding officer presented a copy or actual communication reasonably advised the respondent.

headings.title: Prohibition on implied civil cause of action for enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in this section shall be interpreted as creating a civil cause of action for damages to enforce its provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all four subsections and subdivisions for 534.604. Preserved mandatory 'shall arrest' in subsection 1 and noted deemed-notice rules in subsection 3.
